description: Internal routes of the fgos host for the run supervisor. Not in help, not user verbs. Only the payload of the same release calls them; a protocol mismatch fails closed with host-version-mismatch (same exit code as the holder-lock internal routes).

common.protocol: --protocol 1 is required on every route; absent or != 1 -> exit 3, stdout {"v":1,"protocol":1,"result":"error","code":"host-version-mismatch"}
common.stdout: machine output only, one JSON object per line, each with v:1 and protocol:1; stderr is free text, never parsed

exitCodes.65: envelope-invalid (missing, v != 3, digest mismatch, GO mismatch)
exitCodes.71: supervise only: attempt-already-bound (supervisor-binding.json or receipt.json exists; nothing was touched, the attempt is left to adopt)

fds.3: attempt lock description (inherited, held EX by the controller's scope); set FD_CLOEXEC first
fds.4: dispatch-cwd lease description, present only when envelope.mutation == mutating; set FD_CLOEXEC first
fds.stdio: stdin /dev/null; stdout and stderr appended to <attemptDir>/supervisor.log by the controller

supervise.process: the controller spawns it with setsid, detached, no IPC channel; it outlives the controller
supervise.windows: one flow, platform parts only: no inherited lock (the supervisor takes attempt.lock, and the lease named by envelope.cwdLeaseFile when mutating, after reading the envelope; the controller must have released them); the GO channel is a named pipe the supervisor listens on before the gate starts (gate --go-socket, --job-name from the driver); the supervisor is the keeper in the declared windows-job record; the same record is declared on the cwd lease file, because both locks die with the supervisor while the agent lives on in the job and a later holder of either must wait for the domain to be empty; the stop is stop-requested.json only (the gate polls it, no signal); steps start through the handle-list spawn with their own kill-on-close job
sequence: declare_domain on the attempt lock (predecessor.v1.json record) before the domain has a process
socketpair for GO; spawn_in(domain, gate spec) with fd map {3: attempt, 4: cwd (if any), 5: GO end}
publish supervisor-binding.json; send GO after HELLO
watch: soft deadline, idle (agent-protocol activity), cancel-requested.json, gate exit
on stop: publish stop-requested.json then SIGTERM the gate; kill_all(domain, gateKillGraceMs) if the gate outlives the grace
gate exited: close fd 4 at once; publish receipt.json; run the steps (step-receipt.v1.json); publish closed.json; exit 0

fds.3: attempt lock description (inherited); set FD_CLOEXEC first
fds.4: dispatch-cwd lease description when mutating; set FD_CLOEXEC first
fds.N: GO channel end (direct); set FD_CLOEXEC first

gate.linux-gate: runs as pid 1 of a fresh pid namespace: bwrap <bwrapPrefix> --unshare-pid --as-pid-1 --proc /proc ... -- <hostBin> internal gate ...; no --die-with-parent in direct mode; installs SIGTERM and SIGINT handlers; reaps with waitpid(-1) continuously
gate.go-socket: GO channel by path. Windows: a named pipe (\\.\pipe\<name>) the supervisor listens on before it spawns the gate; the gate connects, sends HELLO, waits for GO. Frames as on --go-fd. Unix terminal mode: the same flag names an AF_UNIX socket path (gate-go.v1.json terminal). --go-fd and --go-socket are exclusive; --go-fd is direct mode only.
gate.windows-job: the supervisor spawns the gate suspended into the attempt's named job, then resumes it; the gate is a member. --job-name <name> is required: the gate opens the job by name (a second holder, so the attempt survives the supervisor), checks it is a member, and runs the agent suspended inside a nested kill-on-close job of its own (so ending the agent's tree never ends the gate). No pid 1 and no signals: the stop request is stop-requested.json, polled every 20 ms (a valid file for this attempt: before GO the gate exits 64, after GO it begins the stop; the cause is the file's cause); the polite stop is a console break to the agent's process group when the gate has a console; after gateKillGraceMs the agent's job is terminated. The hard ceiling is on GetTickCount64 milliseconds since boot (boottimeNs = ms * 1e6; bootId cannot be read on Windows and is not compared). Agent gone: terminate the nested job, wait up to 10 s for the attempt job to hold only the gate, publish gate-exit.json (exitCode is the OS exit code, signal is always null; an agent ended by the gate shows exit code 1), exit 0. --lock-fds is refused: the lock is scoped to the job.
gate.macos-tree: not pid 1, no subreaper: the agent runs in its own session and group; when it exits the gate kills the agent's group and, while the agent's identity still resolves, its process tree (domain_kill_all macos-tree), and waits up to 10 s for the domain judge to report empty. A descendant that left the group (setsid, double fork) and was reparented to launchd is the named escape of this driver.
sequence: CLOEXEC lock fds and the GO fd
read and verify the envelope; send HELLO; wait for GO (EOF before GO -> exit 64 without running the agent)
open capture files (dup2 to 1, 2) and stdin per launch.stdinPolicy
spawn the agent (setsid inside the namespace) with env = launch.env + sideFile.env; send AGENT
wait: agent exit, SIGTERM/SIGINT (forward SIGTERM to the agent group, SIGKILL after gateKillGraceMs), hard ceiling on CLOCK_BOOTTIME (same SIGTERM -> grace -> SIGKILL)
agent gone: kill(-1, SIGKILL), reap until ECHILD, publish gate-exit.json, exit 0

exitCodes.64: no GO: the agent was never started

adopt.scan: stdin: one absolute attemptDir per line; stdout: one JSON line per attemptDir in input order
adopt.probeOnly: report state only, write nothing, take no lock (LOCK_SH|LOCK_NB probe)

stdout.pendingStep: stepId the adopter could not finish (state open)

stateMeaning.running: the attempt lock is held and no adopting.json names the holder; on Windows also reason `starting`: lock free, no binding or receipt, envelope `createdAt` younger than 60 s on this boot (the supervisor takes the lock itself, so the lock is free between the controller letting go and the binding)
stateMeaning.being-adopted: the attempt lock is held by an adopter (adopting.json present)
stateMeaning.needs-adopt: probe-only: lock free and domain empty, not closed
stateMeaning.held: the lock is free but the domain its holder declared could not be emptied within the kill wait (reason predecessor-domain-not-empty): nothing was done
stateMeaning.adopted: this call took the lock and drove the attempt to closed
stateMeaning.open: this call took the lock but a step returned retry or failed; the attempt stays for a later adopt
stateMeaning.closed: closed.json present (skipped without probing the lock)
stateMeaning.legacy-run: no attempt.lock or no envelope v3: not this door's run (the legacy sweep, src/run-supervisor/legacy-sweep.mjs, settles it)

adopt.rule: lock free is not enough: adopt proceeds only when containment.is_empty(binding.domain) == empty (unknown counts as not empty)

attempt-step.execution: the host execs the Node payload of envelope.payloadRoot (resolved like apps/fgos/src/legacy_exec.rs, never PATH) with entry src/run-supervisor/attempt-step.mjs, passing stepId and the attemptDir

exitCodes.75: retry (EX_TEMPFAIL): no receipt, adopt runs the step again later

lock-scan.stdin: one absolute lock file path per line
lock-scan.stdout: one JSON line per path in input order: {path, state: free|held|missing}
lock-scan.method: open O_RDWR, flock(LOCK_SH|LOCK_NB), close; never LOCK_EX so two scans never block each other
